title: Module stalk comparison and geometric-fibre restriction factorization
statement: Let f:X -> Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, s:Spec Omega -> Y a geometric point with Omega algebraically closed, F an etale sheaf of Lambda-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and (g′:X′ -> X,f′:X′ -> Spec Omega,f,s) Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let A be the pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with any IsLocalRing structure, and rho:Spec A -> Y its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put T=X times_Y Spec A, with projections q:T -> X and p:T -> Spec A. There exist t:Spec Omega -> Spec A with t rho=s and image the closed point, and i:X′ -> T with i q=g′ and (i,f′,p,t) Cartesian. There are module isomorphisms Theta:(f_*F)_s -> Gamma(T,q^*F) and b:Gamma(X′,i^*q^*F) -> (g′^*F)(id_X′), such that for every pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v) and section z in F(V times_Y X), b applied to restriction along i of Theta(germ(z)) equals the inverse-image unit restriction along the iterated pullback lift with projections (f′ followed by v,g′) and id_X′. This statement asserts no injectivity of the restriction along i and imposes no integral or proper hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 03Q9 and 03Q1; strict henselization construction in Tag 04HX

proof.text: Construct the cocone of coordinate rings mapping to global sections of Spec Omega by the marked neighbourhood maps. Its colimit desc, followed contravariantly by Spec and the Gamma-Spec unit, defines t. The coprojection-desc identity and Gamma-Spec naturality show t followed by every affine limit leg is the marked map. Nonemptiness of the affine pointed index and the structural-map characterization give t rho=s.

Apply the closed-fibre equivalence with A equal to the strict-henselization ring and the identity spectrum isomorphism to t(closedPoint Omega). Its premise follows from t rho=s. Define i by pullback.lift with projections g-prime and f-prime followed by t. Its two projection equations hold by lift_fst and lift_snd; cancellation of the right Cartesian square proves IsPullback i f-prime p t.

Use exists_qcqsStrictLocalModuleComparison to obtain Theta and its affine representative equations, avoiding a second module/set comparison construction. This previously proved module comparison is a generic tool from the proper-base-change unit; no properness or torsion hypothesis is used.

Import all GeometricFibreExchangeGerms for proof use and apply its existing private theorem terminalGerm_isIso, without restating it: at the identity geometric point every pointed neighbourhood has a marked section, so the terminal germ is bijective. Its inverse, followed by the unique terminal-object pullback isomorphism, defines b-zero from the target stalk to the identity sections. Apply the existing private sourceStalkIso_germ from the same module, without restating it. The exchange-unit equation and the two pullback projection calculations then show that germ followed by sourceIso.inv, exchange, and b-zero equals geometricFibreSectionRestriction on every neighbourhood. The specialized exchange representative helper is proved completely.

Define b as global sections of upperStarComp.inv, the inverse pushforward-global-sections comparison, the terminal-section comparison, the terminal germ isomorphism, and b-zero. Apply strictLocal_exchange_compatibility to the pointed-leg equations, the two projection equations of i, and Theta.hom. Cancel the source stalk isomorphism to identify Theta.hom followed by restriction and b.hom with sourceIso.inv followed by exchange and b-zero.hom. Precompose with an arbitrary germ, use the preceding representative calculation, and evaluate at z. This proves precisely the displayed formula.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03Q9, 03Q1, 04HX and 0EYP; reuse of the qcqs module comparison and strict-local exchange compatibility. Reuse terminalGerm_isIso and sourceStalkIso_germ through a proof-only import all of GeometricFibreExchangeGerms, and specialize its exchange representative calculation to exchange itself.
